This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 03.11.2022 at about 4.45 p.m. to 4.46 p.m. she had been proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EF-2005 being ridden by her husand near Chenduru Cross, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura, at that time, a Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-0462 being driven by its driver with high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle, due to the said impact,
she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she has taken first aid treatment, thereafter shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, further she has taken treatment at Jain Mission Hospital as inpatient and towards the medical expenses she has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-, further she SCCH-5 has spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.50,000/- towards attendant charges.
3. Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 41 years, working as tailor, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to move her leg, unable to do her business and she has suffered 100% physical disability.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver and Gudibande Police have registered a case in crime No.182/2022 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the insurer and 2nd Respondent being the R.C.Owner of the offending Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier Vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.12,00,000/-
to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 18% p.a. SCCH-5 4.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Further admitted that it has issued policy of insurance in respect of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B- 0462 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further submitted that, alleged accident was occurred due to carelessness and negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-EF- 2005 in which petitioner was travelling, the rider of the said motor cycle ridden the Radhamma N vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140559182/
2 vehicle in rash and negligent manner and petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
Further submitted that, petitioner is liable to dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties SCCH-5 i.e., insured and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EF-2005.

Further denied age,
occupation and income of the petitioner and submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Respondent No.2 also appeared through his counsel and filed written statement in which he denied the entire case of the petitioner and he admits about validity of policy for the date of accident and prays to dismiss the petition with cost.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the SCCH-5 motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.11.2022 at about 4.45 p.m. to 4.46 p.m.
near Cenduru Cross, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura due to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-B-0462 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove her case, petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not lead their evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative SCCH-5 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner inorder to prove her case, she himself examined as PW-1 and in her chief- examination evidence, she has reiterated petition averments.
Though he has been elaborately cross- examined by the Respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.4, copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.6.
SCCH-5 11.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, mahazar,
IMV Report, wound certificate and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 03.11.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
12.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 03.11.2022 at about 4.45 p.m. to 4.46 p.m. when he was travelling as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-EF-2005 being ridden by her SCCH-5 husband near Chenduru Cross, Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
13. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of Mahindra Bolero Goods Carrier vehicle.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

14. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 41 years, for proof of her age,
she has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, SCCH-5 wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1981 and the alleged accident was occurred on 03.11.2022,
accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 her age is considered about 42 years as on the date of accident.

Further she was working as Tailor and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. to prove the said fact,
there are no documents on record.
15. As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained grievous bleeding injuries to right leg and head injury.

In this regard she has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.7 issued by Jain Mission Hospital, Chikkaballapur, wherein she took treatment from 03.12.2022 to 07.12.2022.

Further she has furnished lower limb report marked as Ex.P.8, OPD Record marked as Ex.P.9, advance receipts marked as Ex.P.10, medical SCCH-5 bills marked as Ex.P.11 amounting to Rs.38,288/- and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.13.
On perusal of Ex.P.11, Sl. No.2 is for Rs.500/-, but in the calculation sheet it is shown as Rs.1,200/-.
So after deducting Rs.700/- out of total medical expenses of Rs.38,288/-, petitioner is entitled for Rs.37,588/- towards medical expenses.
16. Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated her nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident.

17. Ofcourse respondent No.1 counsel has filed memo with ruing reported in ILR 2000 KAR 1803 in SCCH-5 between B.H.Rangaiah V/s. H.R.V. Basavaraju and another, in which the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "if a person has not sustained any injuries, then he is not entitled for any compensation", but the ruling is not applicable to the present case on hand, because, the facts and circumstances involved in the said case are entirely different from the present set of facts i.e., as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two simple injuries and she spent certain amount for hospital expenses as stated above.

sentences.text: 18. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.87,588/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
SCCH-5 19.
Though the Respondents have taken several defence in their respective written statement, but whatever defence taken by them is not at all established by leading evidence.
In other words, the respondents have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The Respondent No.1 in its written statement admits that, it has issued policy with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-B-0462 which is valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the R.C.Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as discussed above, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date SCCH-5 of accident.
hence the respondent No.1 Insurance Company shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

20. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.87,588/- (Rupees Eighty Seven Thousand Five Hundred Eighty Eight Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
